question: Can ilmenite or a tin-processing secondary resource support a new fully reviewed microbial mechanism record?
decision: Source-only deferral; no new record/history event.

search_limit: No correction/retraction notice was identified in these returned sets or the retrieved Crossref update-to/relation fields. This is a bounded result, not proof of absence.

source_assessments.title: Titanium and iron dissolutions from ilmenite by acid leaching and microbiological oxidation techniques
source_assessments.edition: Asia-Pacific Journal of Chemical Engineering 8(3), May 2013, 323–330; publisher indexed first publication 4 May 2012
source_assessments.scope: Ilmenite concentrate from tin tailings; original main methods/tables/figures unavailable. Publisher and institutional abstracts/metadata were inspected; Crossref request returned429.
source_assessments.reason: Cannot establish full microbial controls, mineral/sample identity and outcome accounting from the abstract. High acid-leaching yields are not biological effects.
source_assessments.rights: Publisher copyright; institutional portal all rights reserved. No redistribution license verified.

source_assessments.title: Bioleaching of ilmenite and basalt in the presence of iron-oxidizing and iron-scavenging bacteria
source_assessments.edition: International Journal of Astrobiology 12(2), April 2013, 123–134; published online11December2012 verified in Crossref
source_assessments.scope: Publisher and institutional abstract plus Crossref identity inspected. Institutional document is a Citation, with link to publisher; full methods not acquired.
source_assessments.reason: Abstract reports no measurable ilmenite Fe/Ti release enhancement relative to abiotic controls. Basalt outcomes and Fe oxidation cannot be assigned to enhanced ilmenite dissolution.
source_assessments.rights: Cambridge copyright; Crossref links general publisher terms, not an open reuse license.

source_assessments.title: Bioleaching of lunar and Martian planetary simulants and ilmenite in the presence of iron-oxidizing bacteria
source_assessments.edition: GSA Denver Annual Meeting2010, Abstracts with Programs42(5), p89, Paper8
source_assessments.scope: Complete original conference abstract inspected; preliminary results, not full methods.
source_assessments.reason: Claims increased ilmenite Fe release whereas later journal abstract reports a null Fe/Ti enhancement result. Related authors/program; independent replication or matched assay identity is not established.
source_assessments.rights: GSA2010 copyright with limited individual scientific-copy permission; full text is not committed.

criticality: Not assessed or asserted; elemental titanium criticality does not transfer to an ilmenite or tailing feed.
dataset: No experimental dataset acquired; schema/data dictionary/keys/missingness and bulk license not assessable. No importer or quantitative observation proposed.
handoff: Acquire legitimate full articles for both verified DOIs; check all original figures, tables, supplements and controls.
Resolve purified mineral versus tin-tailing/concentrate identity and verify any proposed root identifier at its authority.
Reconcile2010preliminary versus2013journal ilmenite claims without pooling basalt assays or counting related outputs as independent studies.
Keep dissolution, Fe oxidation, secondary sequestration and isolated-product recovery distinct. Preserve null results when curation becomes possible.
